note: Four ways to dress cabbage, three of them drawn from a published recipe and one composed from the record's own description. Quantities scale off the cabbage, not the bowl.
carolina_note: Chop finer than instinct says. Eastern pits mince it near as small as the meat so the two marry on the bun; Lexington pits chop fine and stain it with the dip. Dress ahead, chill until it weeps.

kinds.name: White slaw
kinds.region: Eastern North Carolina and most of South Carolina
kinds.says: Mayonnaise, sugar, vinegar. Cut fine so it mixes with the meat on the bun.

anchor.note: Composed from the record's cited description — mayonnaise or whipped dressing, sugar, vinegar, salt, pepper, sometimes carrot or onion. Wikibooks' coleslaw skips the sugar that defines this one, so its proportions are not borrowed here.

steps: Chop the cabbage fine — finer than feels right.
Whisk the dressing until the sugar dissolves.
Fold it through and chill it two hours. It weeps; drain or stir.

kinds.name: Red slaw
kinds.says: Cabbage stained with the pit's own dip. No mayonnaise anywhere near it.

anchor.note: Composed from the record's cited description: vinegar, ketchup, sugar, salt, black pepper, or a ladle of the house dip. Build the dip on the sauce tab and spoon that over instead — the pits do.

steps: Stir the dressing cold until the sugar goes.
Turn it through until the cabbage takes the colour, then chill it.
kinds.swap: Or ladle over the Lexington dip you built on the sauce tab and skip the dressing here.

kinds.name: Yellow slaw
kinds.region: Scattered across the Coastal Plain and the Midlands
kinds.says: Takes mustard into the dressing, and turns the colour of the sauce belt around it.

anchor.note: The white-slaw record notes only that a yellow slaw takes mustard in the dressing. Proportions here are this project's own.

steps: Whisk mustard into the mayonnaise first, then the rest.

kinds.name: A boiled dressing, 1879
kinds.region: The ancestor both slaws descend from
kinds.says: Eggs, vinegar and butter cooked to a custard, poured over cold cabbage. Predates the mayonnaise jar.

anchor.title: Dressing for Cold Slaw
anchor.note: Marion Cabell Tyree's receipt, in its own quantities: a cup of vinegar, two eggs well beaten, a teaspoonful each of salt and mustard, a tablespoonful each of sugar and butter, a little black pepper. It dresses about a head of cabbage.

steps: Mix butter, salt, pepper, sugar and mustard; add the eggs last.
Boil the vinegar and pour it on, stirring the whole time.
Return it to the pan, boil a few minutes, cool it, and pour it over the cabbage.
